function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete REST‑API call** you can use to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you prefer the `gcloud` CLI, see the short snippet at the end.)

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | What you need |
|------|---------------|
| **Project ID** | Your GCP project identifier (e.g., `my-gcp-project`) |
| **Zone** | The zone where you want the instance (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| **Authentication** | OAuth 2.0 access token with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope |
| **GPU API enabled** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| **Billing enabled** | The project must have billing attached |
| **GPU driver installation** | The instance will automatically install the NVIDIA driver via metadata (see below) |

> **Tip:**  
> The NVIDIA driver installation is handled by the Compute Engine metadata key `install-nvidia-driver=true`.  
> The driver version is automatically chosen by Google; you can override it with `nvidia-driver-version=470` if you need a specific version.

---

## 2. REST API Call

### Endpoint

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your values.

### Request Body (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20230912"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "install-nvidia-driver",
        "value": "true"
      },
      {
        "key": "nvidia-driver-version",
        "value": "470"
      },
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### cURL Example

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> Save the JSON above to `instance.json` and run the cURL command.  
> The `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` command fetches a fresh OAuth token for you.

---

## 3. Quick `gcloud` CLI Alternative

If you prefer the CLI, the same instance can be created with:

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --metadata install-nvidia-driver=true,nvidia-driver-version=470 \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470'
```

---

## 4. What Happens After Creation?

1. **Boot Disk** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS is installed on the boot disk.  
2. **GPU** – The RTX A6000 is attached and the NVIDIA driver is automatically installed.  
3. **Networking** – The instance gets an external IP via NAT.  
4. **Service Account** – The default service account is used with full Cloud Platform scope.  

You can SSH into the instance once it’s running and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu20@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with the driver version you requested.

---

### Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU not available** | Ensure the zone supports the GPU type (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). Use `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone us-central1-a` to check. |
| **Billing error** | Verify billing is enabled for the project. |
| **Driver install fails** | Check the serial console logs (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`). |
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase in the GCP console. |

---

That’s it! With the JSON body above (or the `gcloud` command), you can programmatically spin up a Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
